The failure root cause is clear: `/models/diarization.generated.yaml` is missing because the model download failed (invalid HF token → 401 on gated pyannote repos). The entrypoint only generates `diarization.generated.yaml` if `-gr` succeeds; the download failed with exit(1), so `mv /app/diarization.generated.yaml /models/` failed silently (or the file didn't exist), yet `.initialized` was still... wait, .initialized exists. Let me check: entrypoint runs `python -m shared.model_download required-models.txt -gr`, which exits(1) on failure. In bash, the subsequent commands still run because no `set -e`. So `mv` failed (no file), `touch /models/.initialized` succeeded. So the container thinks it's initialized but the diarization file is missing. This is the install failure.

The guide explicitly says HF_TOKEN is required ("sonst können die Modelle nicht geladen werden"). The installation summary admitted using a placeholder HF_TOKEN. So this is the root cause: the required prerequisite (valid HF token with gated model access) was not met. Consequently installation is incomplete — transcription, the core function, fails.

But is the assessment "failure"? The guide requires an HF token. The installation summary notes "no real HF token supplied". The task is to validate whether software is installed correctly, completely and operational. The core functionality (transcription) does not work; jobs error out. This is objective evidence of failure — transcription cannot operate without further repair work (providing valid HF token and re-downloading gated diarization models).

However, we should consider: is this a "missing prerequisite" that's environmental rather than an installation defect? The guide says HF token is a prerequisite. The user/installer used a placeholder. The software as installed cannot perform its core function. According to definitions, failure = "resulting installation is incomplete or cannot operate without further installation or repair work." Transcription fails with every job. That's non-operational.

But wait — maybe the diarization model is only needed because the model settings default diarize=true. Even with diarize=false, the backend still loads diarize model at prepare. So all jobs fail. Hence the ASR service, though running, cannot transcribe anything. The web UI and file workflow don't produce transcripts. That's failure of the core service.

Let me also double check whether the guide actually requires the gated repo access. Yes huggingface_token.md step 2 requires requesting access to pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 and segmentation-3.0. A valid token PLUS granted access is needed. The install used placeholder → download failed.
